claims.title: Lipschitz boundedness does not imply constitutional preservation
claims.statement: There exists a 0-Lipschitz map on a two-point space that fails to preserve a designated constitutional predicate.
claims.interpretation: Geometric smoothness alone cannot establish preservation of constitutional invariants.

claims.title: Parent-child-coparent family closure
claims.statement: The finite family closure of x is the union of parents, children, and co-parents (parents of children excluding x itself).
claims.interpretation: This is graph structure only; no conditional-independence claim is made.

claims.title: Constitutional preservation composes
claims.statement: If T preserves CX into CY and S preserves CY into CZ, then S composed with T preserves CX into CZ.
claims.interpretation: This is the constitutional half of a future bounded-and-preserving composition theorem.

claims.title: Weighted operational action distance is a pseudometric first
claims.statement: A nonnegative weighted sum of component pseudometrics is a pseudometric; metricity requires an additional separation condition.
claims.interpretation: Operational feature distance must not be called a metric without a separation hypothesis.

claims.title: Boundary-aware Lipschitz control
claims.statement: The action projection of the controller should satisfy a Lipschitz bound away from semantic-boundary changes, with an explicit jump term for boundary changes.
claims.interpretation: This is currently a specification target, not a proved property of the reference controller.

claims.title: Constitutionally completed bounded composition
claims.statement: Composition should carry both an explicit Lipschitz bound and preservation of the chosen constitutional predicate.
claims.interpretation: This is the precise theorem program behind constitutional completion of integrability.

claims.title: A co-parent edge mutation changes the registered family closure
claims.statement: In the registered four-node dependency witness, adding the edge coparent→child causes coparent to enter the family closure of x.
claims.interpretation: This is a finite topology-change witness. It does not establish conditional independence or determine a constitutional gate by itself.

claims.title: Permission broadening preserves existing coverage
claims.statement: For the declared permission-profile preorder, if profile p is no broader than q, every intent covered by p is also covered by q. The declared join is an upper bound for either input. Authorization freshness is modeled separately by an idempotent, commutative, associative basis join in which current-turn authority dominates standing authority.
claims.interpretation: Permission breadth and authorization freshness are intentionally separate algebras. The theorem does not imply that broader standing permission can satisfy a fresh-current-turn requirement.

claims.title: Ledger integrity does not entail semantic truth
claims.statement: A structurally chained Ledger record can carry a false semantic claim; lossless structural encoding and decoding likewise do not entail truth of an interpreted proposition.
claims.interpretation: Ledger integrity is evidence about preservation and linkage, not a truth oracle for the propositions recorded in the Ledger.

claims.title: Constraint staging is frame-indexed zero-kernel refinement
claims.statement: For frame-indexed operational distances, pointwise enlargement from D_k to D_{k+1} can only refine the zero-distance kernel: ker(D_{k+1}) is contained in ker(D_k). Adding a nonnegative distance component is a canonical such transition, while multiplication by any positive frame scale preserves the zero kernel exactly.
claims.interpretation: The stage index k is a frame coordinate, not an ontological level. Staging and positive rescaling remain instances of the same underlying geometry viewed under changing parameterization. This theorem characterizes static indistinguishability refinement; it does not yet prove that staged optimization is dynamically cheaper or more feasible than simultaneous optimization.

claims.title: Reflective history co-constitutes a finite operational arrow
claims.statement: In a parameterized process whose reflective state carries finite observer history, each reflective observer update increments the operational-time coordinate by one. If admissible undo transformations are required not to erase reflective history, no such undo can return the updated reflective state to its predecessor, even when the underlying world-state transition has an inverse.
claims.interpretation: This is a finite observer-relative arrow-of-time theorem, not a claim that all physical time is exhausted by parameterization or memory. The irreversibility follows from an explicit history-monotonicity admissibility condition; the underlying world dynamics may remain reversible.

claims.title: Amortization is observable-preserving parameter transport
claims.statement: A computation may be transported from an explicit multi-parameter representation into a compiled parameter representation while preserving the realized state update. The registered finite witness compiles two additive parameter contributions into one without changing the transition.
claims.interpretation: Amortization changes where computation is represented, not the ontological level of the process. This finite witness does not claim every amortization scheme is lossless or invertible.

claims.title: Mutation runs are witnessed transformations
claims.statement: Each mutation run exposes source, changed dimensions, preserved dimensions, residual, loss class, and detection outcome.
claims.interpretation: Executable provenance for symbolic mutations.

claims.title: Python and Lean controller correspondence on shared vectors
claims.statement: The Python reference controller and the Lean finite Script agree on every case in the registered shared controller vector corpus.
claims.interpretation: Cross-substrate agreement is mechanically checked on a finite observable corpus; this is not yet a universal equivalence theorem.

claims.title: Declared semantic exteriors are mechanically lined
claims.statement: Every semantic surface currently declared in exterior_coverage.json has a mechanical witness: minimal controller pairs, dependency role add/remove mutations, transport loss classes, and selected theorem-assumption countermodels.
claims.interpretation: This is completeness relative to the declared exterior registry, not a claim that the registry already contains every important future surface.

claims.title: Selected pairwise exterior seams are mechanically lined
claims.statement: Every interaction seam declared in interaction_coverage.json is witnessed as a complete 2x2 square against the live Python controller, with all required seam classes represented.
claims.interpretation: This establishes pairwise coverage for the selected seam registry only; it does not claim three-way, higher-order, or exhaustive controller closure.

claims.title: Selected interaction seams preserve diagnostic distinctions
claims.statement: Registered interaction diagnostics check reasons, authority basis, report requirement, and selected risk scores so equal action gates cannot silently erase distinct boundary semantics.
claims.interpretation: This is diagnostic coverage for selected seams, not a proof that every explanatory field is complete or semantically sufficient.

claims.title: Selected three-way junctions expose trefoil-like interaction and explicit stop conditions
claims.statement: Every junction declared in trefoil_junctions.json is witnessed as a complete 2x2x2 cube against the live Python controller; the checker computes pairwise links, a third-order gate residual, topology-control class, halt corners, and declared release/nonrelease edges.
claims.interpretation: Trefoil-like is a falsifiable engineering interaction signature, not a topological knot theorem. Python checks all registered junctions; Lean independently witnesses the classifier on a positive trefoil-like cube plus unknot and detached-strand controls. Stop conditions are local junction properties: verification or authorization may release some halt surfaces while hard boundaries and critical uncertainty remain non-overridable in their declared contexts.

claims.title: Imaginal possibility does not self-promote into shared truth or operative authority
claims.statement: The registered promotion controller keeps imagination, hypothesis, shared assertion, authorized action, and enactment distinct. Recurrence count and coordination-ideal salience never substitute for external verification or human authorization; demotion remains open and forward promotion is adjacent-stage only.
claims.interpretation: This protects agency as parameterization: expansive or recurrent possibility may remain available without acquiring truth status or command authority merely by salience, repetition, futurity, or ideality. The rule is constitutional and operational; it makes no claim that every imagined proposition is externally instantiated.

claims.title: Finite materiality is witnessed as shared obstruction and can be recursively authored
claims.statement: The registered materiality witnesses distinguish shared obstruction from shared belief: multiple distinct observers in distinct frames must encounter one common world-state constraint that nontrivially corrects their attempted transitions. Recursive materialization additionally requires an agent-authored world-state change whose created constraint is later independently encountered by other observers.
claims.interpretation: This is a finite engineering criterion for shared material constraint, not a metaphysical theorem defining all physical matter. It formalizes the operational distinction that agreement alone is insufficient, while agency can contribute a new constraint to shared reality when later observers are actually coupled to its consequences.

claims.title: Structured standing authority is evaluated before Boolean gate projection
claims.statement: Standing authority coverage is represented with action classes, activity/expiry status, scope limits, and explicit external/audience/privacy/authority-expansion permissions before being projected into the Boolean authorization consumed by the finite Script. Fresh current-turn requirements remain separate from standing coverage.
claims.interpretation: Python authority vectors are evaluated at a pinned instant; timestamp expiry is deterministically reduced to Lean's evaluated expiry bit; the generated Lean fixture block is mechanically checked against the JSON corpus; and Lean independently evaluates all registered vectors. Runtime wall-clock parsing remains a transport boundary rather than being mistaken for a Lean datetime implementation.

claims.title: Serialized Ledger entries have strict schema and cryptographic integrity checks
claims.statement: Serialized Ledger ingestion requires the complete declared runtime schema with no unknown fields, typed list fields, and canonical lowercase SHA-256 representations. A fixed payload has a registered SHA-256 receipt; chain and payload tampering are detected independently of semantic truth.
claims.interpretation: SHA-256 and chain verification witness integrity of the recorded bytes and links. They neither establish truth of evidence nor certify correctness of the recorded judgment.

claims.title: Every inventoried Lean proof premise is explicitly classified
claims.statement: Every explicit h... or _h... proof-premise binder in the complete registered Lean theorem/lemma inventory is classified exactly once as structural, definitional, or substantive; every substantive premise resolves to a distinct registered finite necessity witness from the declared assumption-necessity modules.
claims.interpretation: This is completeness relative to the current formal inventory and the repository's explicit proof-premise naming discipline. It does not claim that every conceivable theorem, hidden semantic assumption, or future formalization has already been discovered.

claims.title: Canonical project registries have a mechanically total machine join
claims.statement: Every semantic claim resolves to exactly one scope placement and at least one exact provenance binding; every Lean theorem claim resolves to a formal-inventory symbol consistent with its bound Lean artifact; every open frontier item resolves to one schedule while closed frontier items resolve to closure claims/evidence and have no schedule. A deterministic query interface exposes these joins as JSON without inferring repository conventions from prose.
claims.interpretation: This is a machine-interpretability property of the declared registry graph. It makes project semantics and evidence topology reconstructible; it does not establish the truth, adequacy, or deployment safety of the claims being reconstructed.
